stem: Two nurses have an interpersonal conflict that is affecting team function. Which manager action best supports constructive conflict resolution?

options.A: Facilitate a respectful, structured discussion focused on the concern and workable solutions.
options.B: Automatically side with the nurse who has worked on the unit longer.
options.C: Terminate one or both nurses before attempting a conflict-resolution process.
options.D: Ignore the conflict because interpersonal problems generally resolve without intervention.

rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS mutual-support tools promote respectful, structured conflict management that identifies the concern and moves the team toward a mutually acceptable resolution. Favoritism, punitive action before assessment, and avoidance do not reflect the TeamSTEPPS approach. A is correct.
educational_objective: Use structured, respectful problem solving when staff conflict affects team function.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: TeamSTEPPS — Mutual Support: Tools for Managing Conflict
source_locator: Mutual Support tools — conflict resolution and DESC-style structured discussion
source_claim_supported: Team conflict should be addressed through structured, respectful communication and problem solving rather than avoidance or favoritism.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — conflict resolution, leadership, and team collaboration
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — staff conflict resolution

source_original.stem: Two staff nurses on a unit have an ongoing interpersonal conflict affecting team dynamics, and one nurse privately asks the manager to simply side with them since they've worked together longer than with the other nurse. The nurse manager's appropriate role instead includes:

options.A: Facilitate a fair structured discussion that identifies issues and workable solutions
options.B: Automatically side with the nurse who has the longest relationship with the manager
options.C: Terminate one or both nurses before attempting any structured conflict-resolution process
options.D: Ignore the conflict because interpersonal problems usually resolve without intervention

source_original.rationale: A nurse manager's appropriate role in addressing staff conflict includes facilitating a structured, fair conversation between the involved parties, helping identify underlying issues and potential solutions, while maintaining professionalism and objectivity — proactive conflict management supports a healthier work environment and better patient care outcomes.
source_original.source_detail: Mutual-support/conflict tools emphasize structured, respectful problem-solving rather than favoritism or avoidance; current TeamSTEPPS curriculum; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Removed the relationship/favoritism cue and unsupported outcome claims; retained the TeamSTEPPS-supported structured conflict-resolution action and reduced difficulty to easy.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Structured respectful problem solving is directly consistent with TeamSTEPPS conflict tools.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed explicit request to side with one nurse.
audit_findings.blueprint: Conflict resolution fits Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked TeamSTEPPS mutual-support tools; A remains unique.
